stemBlocks.value: A technician earns $3 200 per week for a 40-hour week. (a) Calculate the hourly rate. (b) Overtime is paid at time and a half; calculate the overtime rate. (c) If the technician worked 6 hours overtime in one week, calculate his total wage for that week.
Think first: Everything here is built from one number, the basic hourly rate, so find that first.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p026-q32 from workbook page 26.

solutionSteps.instruction: Divide the weekly wage by the number of basic hours.
Multiply the basic rate by 1.5 for time and a half.
Calculate the overtime pay for 6 hours.
Add the overtime pay to the basic weekly wage.

strategyBlocks.value: Divide the weekly wage by 40 hours for the basic rate, multiply that by 1.5 for the overtime rate, then add 6 hours of overtime pay to the basic weekly wage.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a) Hourly rate = $80  (b) Overtime rate = $120 per hour  (c) Total wage for the week = $3 920

whyThisWorks.value: Basic pay covers a fixed number of hours and any hours beyond that are paid at an enhanced rate. Time and a half means one and a half times the basic rate, so the multiplier is 1.5. Total wage is basic pay plus overtime pay, never the whole week recalculated at the overtime rate.

examTip.value: Break every wage question into basic hours at the basic rate plus extra hours at the enhanced rate. Two lines of working, then one addition.
